source_title: Towards the Properties of Different Biomass-Derived Proteins via Various Extraction Methods
authors: Lin Du; Pablo J. Arauzo; Maria Fernanda Meza Zavala; Zebin Cao; Maciej Pawel Olszewski; Andrea Kruse
geography: Pasture grass from a farm near Karlsruhe, Germany
evidence_class: Primary experimental literature; pasture-grass extraction and dried-precipitate measurements
measurement_basis: Fresh pasture grass was cut to 2–3 cm and stored at −15 °C. Alkaline and aqueous extraction used a 1:10 solid/liquid ratio, 40 °C and 120 min; alkaline treatment used 0.1 M NaOH and pH >11, aqueous extraction used water at pH 7. Subcritical water extraction used a semi-continuous reactor at 200 °C, 40 bar, 6 mL/min for 20 min. All protein-rich aqueous extracts were adjusted to pH 3.0 using 1 M TCA, centrifuged at 13,500 × g and 4 °C for 20 min, frozen and lyophilized.
uncertainty: Table 1 values are means with n=3 and standard deviations in parentheses; where the table marks SD less than 0.05, that upper bound is preserved rather than replaced with an assumed zero.
conversion_and_scaling: No conversion performed. The source defines protein extraction yield as dried precipitate mass divided by protein content in starting biomass; purity as protein content in dried precipitate divided by dried precipitate mass. Protein was estimated using total nitrogen × 6.25 where direct assays were impractical.
applicability: Pasture-grass comparator for extraction/precipitation method comparisons and product purity; suitable for literature screening across green-biomass contexts after matching feedstock and process boundaries.
limitations: Pasture grass is not roadside/VARTA grass and was frozen before extraction.
The reported protein extraction yield depends on the paper's operational definition and should not be interpreted as a universal recovered-protein coefficient.
TCA precipitation and lyophilization are laboratory procedures, not GreenHub's active commercial process.
No complete stream mass balance, reagent demand per plant throughput, energy demand, or continuous-scale data are reported.
The extract is reference-only and not calculation-connected.
